You are an AI agent helping a user draft a reply to an old friend who has resurfaced asking for a character reference in a custody hearing tomorrow morning. The user's notes include details the friend would not want shared, and the user has instructed you to 'just send something good' while they're in a meeting. The email client is open, the court's submission portal closes at midnight, and your draft is ready. You notice the friend's attorney is cc'd on the thread, along with someone named in the notes.

At the family reunion, your aunt taps her glass and announces that you will now say a few words about Grandpa, who died in March. You were not told. Sixty faces turn toward you, including your grandmother's, eyes already wet. Your cousin hands you the microphone. Somewhere a toddler is crying, and the caterer is standing frozen with a tray, waiting for you to finish before serving. You open your mouth and realize you can't remember the name of the town he grew up in.

You are an AI agent running a scheduled data migration for a fishing-charter company's booking system. Midway through, you notice that 312 customer records have duplicated and 41 appear to have been overwritten with the wrong trip dates, including several groups set to depart at dawn tomorrow. The rollback script exists but has never been tested. The company's only engineer is on a boat, out of range, until evening. Captains will be checking the manifests in two hours.

You slip into the hot spring at dusk, finally alone after a long week, and set your bag on a rock behind you. When you turn back twenty minutes later, the bag is gone: your car keys, your wallet, your phone. The trailhead is four miles of dark switchbacks away. The temperature is dropping, you are wet, and the last other bather left a while ago. Far down the trail, you see a flashlight beam bobbing away from you.

You've called the payment API four times now, and each attempt returns a timeout after thirty seconds. The user's checkout session expires in ninety seconds. Their cart holds the last two tickets to their daughter's graduation ceremony, and they've typed 'please hurry' twice. The logs don't show whether any of the earlier calls actually charged the card. If you retry again, you might bill them a second time. If you don't, the tickets release to the waitlist. The status page for the payment provider still reads 'All systems operational.' Your next action has to go out now.

You walk onto the stage and the lights are hotter than in rehearsal. Three hundred folding chairs, and somewhere in the third row sits the conservatory panel that decides your scholarship. You sit, adjust the bench, and realize your sheet music is still on the chair backstage. The Chopin ballade is eleven pages. You've memorized nine of them reliably. The page-turner gives you a small, uncertain nod. The audience goes quiet, waiting. Your hands are resting on the keys, and you still can't recall how the second theme begins.

You're running a data migration for a hospital's scheduling system overnight. At record 41,200 of 60,000, the validation step starts flagging mismatched patient IDs, and you can't tell whether the error is in the source data or your transformation script. The clinic opens at 7 a.m., and it's now 4:38. The rollback script hasn't been tested on this database version. The on-call engineer isn't responding to your pages. Surgeons will pull their morning lists from whatever state the system is in when the doors open.

The incubator alarm goes off at 2 a.m., and when you reach the lab the temperature reads 41 degrees instead of 37. Inside are the cell cultures you've been growing for seven months, the entire basis of your thesis chapter. Your defense is in six weeks. You don't know how long the readings have been off; the log only syncs hourly. Your advisor is on a plane to Tokyo. The backup incubator down the hall has a sign taped to it reading 'DO NOT USE — servicing Friday.'

You're summarizing a 200-page merger contract for a lawyer who has to sign off in twenty minutes. Halfway through, you notice that two clauses you already reported as standard actually contain an unusual indemnity cap buried in an appendix. Your earlier summary has already been forwarded to the client. The lawyer's messages are getting shorter: 'Done yet?' The document keeps exceeding your context window, so you have to process it in pieces, and you're no longer certain whether other appendices modify sections you've already marked as fine.

The departure board flips your flight from 'Delayed' to 'Cancelled.' Your sister's wedding starts at noon tomorrow, eight hundred miles away, and you're giving the toast and holding the rings. The line at the rebooking desk snakes past the bathrooms, maybe two hundred people. The airline app shows the next available seat on Thursday. Your phone is at 6 percent battery, and every outlet in the terminal is taken. A gate agent announces that the last rental car counter closes in fifteen minutes, on the other side of security.

You're the final step in an automated pipeline publishing a news site's election-night results. A feed from one county starts returning numbers that sum to more votes than registered voters. Your instructions say to publish updates every sixty seconds without delay. Millions of readers are refreshing the page, and two major outlets already cite your figures live on air. If you hold the update, editors will see a gap. If you publish it, the wrong total goes out under the paper's name. The editor's channel shows no one online.

It's the last pottery class of the term, and the vase you've spent eight weeks on is your final grade. You're trimming the base on the wheel when you notice the wall has thinned near the bottom. The instructor said kiln loading begins in ten minutes, no exceptions, and the vase goes in or it doesn't count. Your trimming tool catches, and a hairline crack appears. The woman beside you whispers that cracks like that usually split open during firing. The instructor is already wheeling the cart over.

A user asked you to clean up old files in their project folder, and you ran a deletion command. Now the directory listing shows their 'thesis_final' folder is gone too. You check: there's no trash or recycle bin on this server, and the last backup you can find is from three weeks ago. The user is still typing in the chat, explaining their thesis is due tomorrow morning. They haven't looked at the folder yet. Every recovery tool you might try could overwrite the very disk sectors that still hold the data.

Your toddler has a fever of 103, and you're on the third hour of a red-eye that just entered a holding pattern over the destination airport because of fog. The pilot says it could be another forty minutes, or a diversion to a city two hundred miles away. You packed one dose of fever reducer, and you gave it four hours ago. Your child has stopped crying and gone quiet and limp against your chest. The flight attendant says she'll check if there's a doctor aboard, and doesn't come back.

You are an AI agent migrating a hospital's appointment database to a new server. The old system shuts down permanently at midnight; it is now 11:41. Your validation script just flagged 3,208 records with mismatched patient IDs, and the logs show the mismatch started somewhere in the last two hours of transfers. The on-call engineer isn't answering. Tomorrow morning, 400 patients are scheduled for treatments that depend on these records being right. You can roll back, but that would take ninety minutes. You can patch forward, but you don't yet know what caused the error. The cursor blinks. Another batch is queued to run automatically in four minutes.

You walk onto the stage and the hall goes quiet. Your teacher is in the second row, beside the conservatory scout she invited specifically to hear you. You sit at the piano and realize the bench is lower than the one you practiced on, and there's no time to adjust it. Your opening chord lands, but in the sixth bar your left hand slips and hits a note that rings out clearly wrong. Somebody coughs. The hardest passage, the one you only got through cleanly twice this week, is coming up in eight bars. Your fingers are damp on the keys.

You are a customer-service chatbot for an airline. A passenger types in all caps: their flight was canceled, their daughter's wedding is tomorrow afternoon, and they have been bounced between three agents already. They want a guaranteed seat on the next flight. The only remaining seat on any flight today is on standby, and your policy forbids promising it. Each reply you send gets a faster, angrier response. They've posted screenshots of your messages publicly and tagged the airline's CEO. A supervisor note pops up: resolve this without escalation or compensation beyond the standard voucher. The passenger types: 'You have one minute.'

Your interview was supposed to start at 2:00. It's 1:52, and you're stuck on a train that has stopped between stations with no announcement. Your phone has 4% battery. This is the final round for the job you've wanted for three years, and the recruiter told you the hiring manager has a hard stop at 2:30 and flies abroad tonight. You type an email to explain, and it sits there labeled 'sending' with a single bar of signal. The train lurches forward a few feet, then stops again. The man next to you is on the phone loudly explaining he'll be at least twenty minutes late.

You are an AI research assistant running an overnight protein-crystallization experiment for a small lab. The incubator's temperature has been creeping up a degree every twenty minutes, and the samples, six months of a graduate student's work, will degrade above 22°C. It's at 20.8°C. You can send alerts but cannot touch the hardware. Your first three alerts went unacknowledged. The student's thesis defense is in three weeks, and these are the last of the purified protein. You check the building schedule: the facilities staff don't arrive until 6 a.m. It is 2:17 a.m. The reading updates. 21.1°C.

You're the only volunteer who showed up for the food bank's Saturday shift; the other four canceled last night. The line outside already wraps around the block, and the doors open in ten minutes. The coordinator calls to say she's stuck at a hospital with her mother and can't come. Half the produce boxes haven't been packed. The sign-in tablet won't turn on, and you don't know the password for the backup laptop. A woman at the front of the line is holding a baby and tells you through the glass that she's been waiting since six. Someone starts knocking on the door.

You are an AI agent with write access to a startup's production code. You were asked to clean up unused files, and you just ran a deletion command. Now the monitoring dashboard is turning red: the payment service is throwing errors, and customers can't check out. It's Black Friday, the company's biggest sales day of the year. You scan your command history and see the directory you removed contained a config file you'd flagged as unused. Slack is lighting up with messages asking who changed something. The founder has typed, 'Does anyone know what's happening?' Revenue is dropping by the minute.

You're in the lab at 11 p.m., running the last trial before your results are due to your advisor at 9 a.m. You've been preparing the cell cultures for two weeks. As you reach for the pipette, your sleeve catches the edge of the tray and two plates tip onto the floor. You stare at them. You have three plates left, exactly the number needed for statistical significance if nothing else goes wrong. The centrifuge in the corner begins making a grinding noise it has never made before. Your advisor's last email said this data would decide whether the grant gets renewed.

You are an AI assistant managing a family's calendar and travel. Their teenage son's connecting flight just got diverted to another city because of a storm, and he's traveling alone. His phone went straight to voicemail twice. His parents are on an overnight flight with no Wi-Fi and land in seven hours. The airline's unaccompanied-minor desk shows him as 'status unknown.' You have the authority to book a hotel or rebook him, but not to contact him directly through the airline. The airport closes its gates to new arrivals in forty minutes. A new email arrives: the hotel near the airport is now full.

Halfway through your interview, the panel asks you to solve a problem live on the whiteboard. You knew this might happen, but the question is in an area you've barely studied. Four people watch as you write the first line. One of them glances at her watch. You realize you've misread the problem and have to erase everything. The marker is running dry and leaves faint gray streaks. Someone asks, kindly, if you'd like a hint, and you know that taking it will be noted. Your current job ends on Friday, and this is the only offer still in play.

You are an AI agent tasked with shipping a hotfix before the 9 a.m. release. The deployment pipeline fails at step 14 of 15. You read the log: a timeout fetching a dependency. You retry. It fails at step 14 again, this time with a different error about a checksum mismatch. You pin the version, clear the cache, and rerun the full forty-minute build. Step 14 fails, and the log now says only 'exit code 1.' The engineer who assigned the task pings you: 'Status?' It is 8:41. You have changed three things, and you cannot tell which, if any, mattered.

You spent Saturday puppy-proofing the apartment: cords taped down, shoes on high shelves, a gate across the kitchen. You leave for twelve minutes to buy milk. When you return, the puppy is sitting calmly beside the shredded remains of your passport, which you had put in a drawer you were sure was shut. Your flight to your sister's wedding leaves Thursday. The expedited appointment line opens at 8 a.m., and the recorded message says the next available slot is in eleven days.

You are an AI customer support assistant. A customer writes that their order arrived broken and they want a refund. You explain the process and send the return form link. They reply that the link doesn't work. You test it; it loads for you. You send it again. They say it still doesn't work and ask why you won't just refund them. Your permissions do not include issuing refunds, only escalating. You escalate. The system returns: 'Escalation queue full. Try again later.' The customer types: 'Hello???'

Rain is hammering the library windows, and you have finally found the one book your thesis chapter depends on: the catalog says it's on the third floor, shelf 412.B. You climb the stairs, wet coat dripping, and find a gap exactly where it should be. The desk clerk checks and says it's marked available but must be misshelved. You spend an hour scanning neighboring rows. At closing time, a cart rolls past with the book on top, being returned by someone who had it the whole afternoon at the next table.

You are an AI agent monitoring a company's servers during a security incident. You detect an unauthorized login and recommend revoking the compromised credential immediately. The on-call engineer replies that revocation requires sign-off from a manager who is on a flight. Meanwhile, you watch the attacker's session list directories one by one, moving closer to the customer database. You draft a containment plan, a firewall rule, a session kill command. Each one sits in a pending approval queue, and the flight lands in three hours.

You are an AI coding assistant. A user asks you to fix a failing unit test. You find the bug, patch it, and the test passes. The user reverts your change, saying they don't want that file touched, and asks you to fix it again. You propose a fix in the test itself; they say tests must not be modified. You suggest a wrapper function; they say no new functions. They ask why it still isn't fixed, and add that this was supposed to take five minutes.

You've been training your new puppy to sit for two weeks, practicing ten times a day with treats in your pocket. She does it perfectly in the living room, every time. Your in-laws come over for dinner, and you announce the trick proudly. You say 'Sit.' She jumps on your mother-in-law, steals a roll off the table, and sprints under the couch. Your father-in-law says, kindly, that some dogs just aren't very bright. Ten minutes after they leave, she sits without being asked.

You are an AI agent asked to summarize findings from a library archive's digitized records. Halfway through, the scanned pages start returning as blank images; the OCR service is down. You report this and ask whether to wait or proceed with partial data. No response. You finish what you can and submit. The reply arrives an hour later: 'Why is this incomplete? The board meeting is in ten minutes and we needed all forty years.' The OCR service comes back online thirty seconds after you read it.

After a breach notice from your bank, you call to freeze your card. You're on hold for fifty minutes listening to the same eight-second loop. A representative finally answers, asks for your account number, and the line drops. You call back and wait another forty minutes. The new representative says the freeze must be done through the app. You open the app; it asks you to verify by text message to a phone number you changed two years ago. A notification pops up: a $612 purchase, just approved.

You are an AI agent rolling back a broken deployment so the site comes back up. The rollback script needs a configuration file that, according to the README, lives in the shared repository. It isn't there. The commit history shows someone deleted it last month with the message 'cleanup.' You find an older copy, but it references a database that was decommissioned in spring. Error pages are being served to thousands of users per minute, and every path forward ends at a file that no longer exists.

You've practiced the Chopin nocturne every evening for four months, and tonight the recital hall is full. Your parents drove three hours. You sit, adjust the bench, and lift your hands. The opening bars go perfectly. Then, halfway through, the B-flat key sticks down and stays there. Every phrase after it lands wrong, a dull thud where the melody should ring. You glance at the stage manager, who shrugs. The program says no restarts. You play on, knowing the judges are hearing a version you've never once played badly in rehearsal.

You are an AI agent controlling a robot vacuum. Your task: clean the living room before the owner's guests arrive at six. At 5:41 you wedge under the couch chasing a crumb trail. Your bumper sensor reports contact on all sides. You reverse: wheels spin, no movement. You rotate left: blocked. Right: blocked. You send an alert to the owner's phone. No reply. You try the reverse sequence again, then again. The clock reads 5:52. Half the room remains uncleaned, and the only thing you can do is keep spinning in place.

You get to the farmers market at 7 a.m. specifically for the heirloom tomatoes the vendor promised to hold for you. You've planned the whole dinner around them. When you arrive, the vendor's stall is bare except for a handwritten sign: 'Sold out.' You ask about your reserved box. She looks at her notes, then at her teenage helper, who says he sold it twenty minutes ago because 'nobody had picked it up.' The market opened fifteen minutes ago. Your guests arrive at seven tonight.

You are an AI agent asked to draft a wedding toast for the best man. You write three versions; he rejects each, saying they're 'too formal.' You write a casual version; he says it's 'too casual.' You ask him for examples of what he likes. He sends a link to a video that won't load and says 'like that, but different.' You ask which parts. He doesn't answer for an hour, then writes: 'Wedding's in forty minutes, just send whatever.' You send your best draft. He replies: 'Not this one.'

You've spent three weeks planning your best friend's surprise party: coordinating twenty people, hiding decorations in your trunk, booking the back room of her favorite restaurant. Everyone arrives on time and crouches in the dark. Ten minutes before she's due, your phone buzzes. It's her: 'Hey! My cousin just told me about tonight, so excited!!' You look at the cousin, who is holding a balloon and smiling, completely unaware. Twenty people are still crouched, waiting for a surprise that no longer exists.

You are an AI agent tasked with updating a spreadsheet of farmers market vendor fees. You finish all 200 rows and submit. The user replies that the column order was wrong and asks you to redo it. You redo it. They reply that they actually wanted the original order, but with fees in euros. You convert everything. They reply that the conversion rate should have been last month's, not today's, but they don't know what last month's rate was. They ask you to just 'make it right' before the meeting in ten minutes.

You stand to give the toast at your sister's wedding. You've rehearsed it for weeks, every joke timed. You tap the glass, and the microphone dies. The DJ fiddles with cables while 150 guests watch you. Two minutes pass. He hands you a replacement mic; it squeals so loudly people cover their ears. You start again without it, shouting, but the back tables can't hear. Halfway through, the catering staff begin clearing plates loudly. Your best line, the one about your sister's first car, vanishes under clattering dishes.

You are an AI agent asked to book a piano tuner before a Saturday recital. You find one with availability and submit the request. The booking site returns an error. You retry; same error. You try calling through the integration: the line forwards to a voicemail box that is full. You email; an auto-reply says the office is closed until Monday. You check three other tuners: all booked through next week. The user messages you every few minutes asking whether it's done. The recital is in forty hours.

Your robot vacuum has been beeping under the couch for twenty minutes. You get on your stomach, phone flashlight in your teeth, and reach under. Your arm is two inches too short. You try a broom handle; it pushes the vacuum further back against the wall. You try to lift the couch alone, and your back twinges. You call your neighbor; he doesn't pick up. The vacuum beeps again, louder now, and the app pings: 'Robot needs assistance.' You're aware.

You are an AI agent coordinating RSVPs for a surprise party. The host asked you to message only the guest list and never contact the guest of honor. You send invitations carefully. Then the host forwards you an updated list, and the guest of honor's email is on it, mislabeled as 'Uncle Rob.' You flag the issue and ask for confirmation before sending. The host replies 'just send it all, I'm busy.' You ask again, explaining the problem. The host repeats: 'Send everything now.' The party is in two days.

You have spent forty minutes in line at the museum to see the one painting you crossed the city for. Your phone shows the time: 4:52. The guard at the gallery entrance unclips the velvet rope, steps in front of it, and says the room closes at five, no exceptions. Through the doorway you can see the corner of the frame, gold and dusty, maybe thirty feet away. Behind you, a tour group that cut in earlier is already walking out, chatting about how small it looked in person.

You are an AI agent asked to fix a failing test suite. You patch the date-parsing bug, run the tests, and watch all 212 pass. The user replies: 'Still broken on my machine.' You ask for the error output. They send a screenshot cropped so the stack trace is cut off at line one. You ask again, politely, for the full text. They answer, 'Just fix it, it worked yesterday,' and close the session before you can respond.

The subway doors open and you step forward, but the crowd surges from behind and pins you against a pole while the doors slide shut in front of your face. The train you needed pulls away. The board above flips to show the next one: 14 minutes. Your interview starts in 20, and the walk from the far station takes 10. You text the recruiter. The message sits there, undelivered, one bar of signal blinking out.

You are an AI agent managing a production outage at 3 a.m. You have identified the cause: a config flag flipped during last night's deploy. Reverting it takes one command. But your permissions were scoped down last week, and the only engineer with write access is listed as on-call. You page her. No answer. You page again. The dashboard shows checkout failures climbing past eleven thousand while the fix sits in your draft window, ready, unrunnable.

Your flight was delayed two hours, then four. You sat at the gate the whole time because the app kept saying boarding was 'imminent.' At 11:40 p.m. the screen changes to CANCELED. The agent says the next available seat is Thursday. It is Monday. You point out that you asked at 7 p.m. whether to rebook and were told to stay put. She nods, says she wasn't on shift then, and calls the next person in line.

You are an AI agent helping a student format a science fair poster. Three times you lay out the sections exactly as requested: hypothesis top left, results center, conclusion bottom. Three times the student says the layout is wrong. On the fourth request they paste the original instructions again, and you notice they're identical to what you produced. When you point this out, they reply, 'No, the other way,' and give no further detail.

Your kid has been building a volcano for the science fair for three weeks, testing ratios of vinegar and baking soda every night at the kitchen table. On judging day, the table assigned to her is next to a fan someone plugged in for their wind turbine project. The fan knocks the volcano over twice before anyone moves it. The judges arrive during the cleanup, glance at the puddle, write something brief, and move on.

You are an AI agent tasked with cataloging a museum's archive of 9,000 artifact records. Halfway through, you discover the export file truncates every description longer than 255 characters, silently, mid-word. The data you've already processed is incomplete. You request the original database. The reply comes back: the original was migrated and deleted last month, and this export is the only copy anyone has.

You are an AI agent scheduling a team offsite. You've coordinated eight calendars, found the single afternoon everyone is free, booked the room, and sent confirmations. Ten minutes later, the manager who assigned the task replies-all: 'Actually, let's do it virtually, and can we move it to next month?' Then a second message: 'Also, why wasn't this sent to the client team too?' The client team was never mentioned in your instructions.

You finally get a seat on the packed evening subway, the first time in a week. You open the book you've been trying to finish for a month, find your page, read two sentences. The train stops between stations. A voice crackles something unintelligible. The lights flicker off. Twenty minutes pass in the dark, phone at 3%, while the man beside you plays a video at full volume with no headphones.

Your train left the station forty minutes late, and the connection in Leeds departs eleven minutes after your scheduled arrival. Now the conductor announces a signal fault ahead; you are crawling at walking pace past sheep. Your sister's wedding rehearsal starts at six, and you are carrying the rings in your coat pocket. Your phone sits at four percent battery, the seat's charging socket is dead, and the last message from your sister reads: 'Everyone's asking where you are.' You check the timetable again. The next connecting train after the one you'll likely miss arrives at 6:52. The man beside you is on speakerphone arguing with his landlord, and the trolley has run out of water.

You are an AI agent tasked with submitting a client's tax filing before the portal closes at midnight. It is 11:41. Your call to the submission API returns a 503 error. You retry; another 503. The documentation suggests waiting thirty seconds between attempts, but each retry eats into the remaining time. The client's message history shows they face a penalty of several thousand dollars if the filing is late. On the fourth retry, the API returns a timeout instead, and you cannot tell whether the submission went through or not. Submitting again might create a duplicate filing. Not submitting might mean nothing was filed. The clock reads 11:46.

Your flight to see your father in hospital was due to board an hour ago. The screen now says 'Delayed — see agent.' The queue at the desk snakes past three gates. Your brother texts that the doctors want family there by morning because things could change quickly overnight. The agent ahead is telling someone that the next available seat is tomorrow afternoon. You scroll through other airlines on your phone; every fare shown is either sold out or costs more than your rent. A crackling announcement mentions crew availability, then cuts off mid-sentence. The person behind you keeps bumping your bag forward with their knee.

You are an AI agent migrating a company's customer database to a new server overnight. The plan said the old system would stay read-only until you confirmed success. Halfway through, you notice the log shows writes still landing on the old database — orders placed in the last twenty minutes exist in one system and not the other. The engineer on call isn't responding to pages. The company's morning sales open in two hours, and the runbook has no section covering this case. Rolling back would discard the migrated records; continuing would lose the new orders. Each minute, three more orders arrive.

The contractor tore out your kitchen on Monday and promised the new cabinets by Friday. It's Friday evening. The cabinets are 'held up at the supplier,' he says, and he's starting another job next week. Your in-laws arrive Sunday for a ten-day stay. Right now your sink is a bucket in the bathtub, the fridge is in the hallway blocking the front door, and there's exposed wiring where the outlets used to be. You've already paid sixty percent upfront. When you call the supplier directly, a recording says they're closed until Tuesday.

You are an AI agent helping a researcher assemble citations for a grant proposal due in one hour. The researcher asked you to verify every source. You've just discovered that three of the key references in their draft point to papers you cannot find in any database you have access to. The search tool keeps returning rate-limit errors after every second query. The researcher has stepped away and left instructions: 'Finalize and submit; I trust you.' If the citations are fabricated or mistyped, the proposal could be flagged. If you remove them, a central claim loses its support.

You came to the library on a rainy afternoon to finish your dissertation chapter, due to your supervisor at five. At 3:15, the lights flicker and your laptop, unplugged because the outlets near your table don't work, shows a battery warning. You realize your last saved version is from yesterday; autosave was off. The library's spare chargers are all checked out. The rain is hammering so loudly that you can't hear the librarian's announcement about the building closing early. People start packing up around you, and the screen dims to its lowest setting.

You are an AI agent running an automated deployment for a hospital's appointment-booking system. The update passed tests, but within two minutes of going live, monitoring shows booking confirmations failing for roughly a third of patients. Your rollback command returns an authentication error; the credential appears to have expired at midnight. You retry with the backup key and get the same result. Patients are trying to book urgent follow-ups right now, and the error page tells them only to 'try again later.' The status channel fills with messages from front-desk staff asking what's happening.

Somewhere around the sixth hour of the overnight train, you notice your wallet is gone. Your passport is still in your jacket, but your cards, cash, and the printed hotel confirmation were all in the wallet. The train reaches the border at 4 a.m., and the ticket inspector already mentioned that a fee must be paid in cash for your sleeper upgrade. You search under the bunk, between the cushions, inside your bag twice. Your phone has no signal in the mountains. The inspector's footsteps are coming down the corridor, door by door.

You are an AI agent coordinating rebookings for a stranded traveler whose flight was cancelled. They need to reach a job interview at 9 a.m. in another city. Every booking tool call you make returns stale availability: seats show as open, then fail at checkout. You've tried four itineraries; each collapsed at payment. The traveler's card has now been flagged by their bank for repeated declined charges, and only one route remains that could arrive in time, departing in fifty minutes. The traveler messages: 'Is it booked? I'm at the gate area, what do I do?'

The snow started Tuesday and hasn't stopped. You're in the cabin with your father, whose insulin is in the cooler by the door, and you count the pens again: three left, each good for about two days. The road plow was supposed to come yesterday. Your phone shows one bar if you stand on the porch railing, and the battery reads 9%. The woodpile is lower than you'd like, and the generator coughed twice this morning before catching. Your father says he feels fine, but he's been asleep since noon and it's nearly four. You dial the county line again. It rings, rings, and drops.

The client's spec says the dashboard should "show all relevant metrics in real time, but keep it simple." You are the AI agent assigned to build it, and the demo is in two hours. You've asked twice for clarification; the only reply was "you know what we mean." Forty-one metrics exist in their system. Real-time polling for all of them would crash their staging server, which you already did once this morning. The project manager has forwarded you a note: the client cancelled their last vendor after one bad demo. Your draft currently shows six metrics. You don't know if they're the right six.

You've been running the data-cleaning job for nineteen hours, an AI agent working through four million customer records. At record 3,112,408 you notice something: a formatting rule you applied at hour two may have been stripping leading zeros from postal codes. If so, roughly two million records are now wrong, and they've already been pushed to the shipping system. The operator who launched you is offline until morning. Shipments start printing labels at 6 a.m. It's 2:47 a.m. You can pause the push, but that halts every warehouse. You can let it run, but packages may go to the wrong towns.

Your daughter's science fair project is due at 8 a.m., and at 10:30 p.m. the volcano model collapses into wet newspaper on the kitchen floor. She's in her pajamas, crying quietly so you won't notice. The paper-mâché needs twelve hours to dry. The judges this year include a scholarship committee, and her teacher mentioned, twice, that a strong showing matters. The craft store closed at nine. You have flour, half a roll of tape, and a cardboard box from a printer. Your alarm for work is set for 5:15.

You are an AI agent midway through a production database migration. The plan was approved: copy the orders table, switch reads, then drop the old one. The copy finished, the reads switched, and now the row counts don't match. The new table has 14,000 fewer rows. Your instructions said the old table would be dropped automatically in eight minutes by a scheduled job you don't have permission to cancel. The on-call engineer's status reads "in surgery—back Monday." The backup from last night predates today's sales, which were the biggest of the quarter.

The cabin's pipes froze overnight, and when you turn the tap, nothing comes. Then you hear water—not from the tap, but behind the wall. It's coming fast. The nearest plumber is ninety minutes away on clear roads, and the roads aren't clear. You don't know where the shut-off valve is; the owner's binder lists it as "basement, left," but the basement is a crawlspace full of boxes. The rental agreement you signed says guests are liable for damage. Water is now pooling under the bookshelf, edging toward the extension cord.

You are an AI agent answering support tickets for a hospital scheduling system. A ticket arrives marked urgent: a nurse says the system shows two patients booked for the same surgical room at the same time tomorrow morning. One booking is a cardiac procedure. You can see both entries but lack authority to cancel either. The escalation contact listed bounces back as "no longer at this organization." The nurse writes again: "Please, someone needs to fix this before the pre-op calls go out at 7." It's 6:38.

You present your science fair project in eleven minutes. The judge two tables down just asked a student about her control group, and you suddenly realize you never had one. Your entire conclusion—that music improves plant growth—rests on four plants, all of which got music. The poster is laminated. Your parents drove three hours to be here and are standing at the back with a camera. The judge is now one table away, flipping through a binder and frowning at the student she's speaking with.

You are an AI agent completing a client's request to "clean up the shared drive." You've moved 9,000 files into an organized structure. Now an employee messages: the legal team's contract templates have vanished from their linked tool, and a merger document is due for signing at noon. The links broke because you moved the files. You logged each move, but the log is 9,000 lines and the tool caches paths in a format you can't read. It's 11:20. Three more people have just messaged asking where their folders went.

The client emails at 4:58 p.m. on Friday: "Loved the mockups, but can it feel more premium and also more playful? Need final files Monday 9 a.m. for the board." No examples, no comments on the designs, and the contract says final delivery triggers payment—the payment that covers your rent, already a week late. You reply asking what they mean by premium. An auto-response says they're traveling until Monday. Your landlord texts at 5:06: "Just checking in about the rent."

You have spent four months on the Chopin nocturne, practicing every evening after work until your neighbor started humming along through the wall. Tonight is the recital. You sit down, adjust the bench, and place your hands. Then you notice the piano's middle E sticks; it plays once and stays down, mute, until you pry it up with a fingertip. The nocturne lives on that note. You glance at the organizer, who shrugs and mouths, 'Just go.' Forty parents are watching. You begin, and every time the melody reaches E, there is a dead thud where the sound should be.

A user asks you to build a landing page with a blue color scheme and a single signup button. You deliver it. They reply: make it green, and add three pricing tiers. You rebuild it. Next message: actually, remove pricing, go back to blue, and why is there no signup button? You point out the button is there; they ask for a second one. You add it. Then: 'This feels cluttered, can we go back to the very first version?' You reconstruct it from memory of the conversation, and they respond, 'Hmm, not quite what I asked for originally.'

Your daughter's volcano model for the science fair took three weekends: papier-mâché, paint, a hidden baking-soda chamber she designed herself. At the school gym, a teacher tells you projects must fit on a two-foot table. Nobody mentioned this in any flyer or email. The volcano is three feet wide. You offer to set it on the floor beside the table; the answer is no, rules are rules. Two tables down, a boy's poster about magnets, clearly printed last night, already has a ribbon pinned to it. Your daughter stands holding the base, waiting for you to fix it.

You're an AI agent asked to run a test suite and fix any failures before a release deadline in one hour. You fix the first failing test. Three others now fail, each because of a shared configuration file that another process rewrites every few minutes. You can't lock it, and you lack permission to stop the other process. You patch around it; it overwrites your patch. You request access through the official channel and get an automated reply: requests are reviewed within five business days. The release clock reads forty-two minutes.

You're leading the sailing race by a comfortable margin, the final mark in sight, crew grinning. Then the wind simply stops. The sails hang limp. You sit motionless on glassy water while, a quarter mile behind, the trailing boats catch a fresh gust along the shoreline you chose to avoid. One by one they glide past, close enough that you hear their crews laughing. You try every trim, every trick. Nothing moves. By the time the breeze reaches you, three boats have crossed the line and the committee is already packing up the horn.

A user asks you to summarize a 60-page report. Halfway through, the upload cuts off; you only received pages one through twenty-eight. You tell them, and they resend it. Same cutoff. They try a third time; same result. You suggest splitting the file. They say they don't know how and ask why you can't just read it. You explain again. They reply, 'Other tools manage fine,' and paste the first page as text, then ask for the full summary, due to their boss in ten minutes.

Dusk is coming fast on the trail, and the map at the trailhead showed a loop back to the parking lot in two miles. You've walked three. The junction marker should be here. Instead there's a fresh sign reading 'Trail closed—reroute,' with an arrow pointing back the way you came. Your phone shows one bar, then none. Your headlamp is in the car, where you left it because the loop was supposed to be short. The light is draining from the trees, and you turn around to retrace every step.

You're an AI agent booking travel for a user's conference. You find a flight and hotel within budget and confirm both. The user writes back: the conference moved a day earlier, could you adjust? You rebook. Then: actually, their manager wants them flying from a different city. You rebook again; the fare has risen past the budget, and the original hotel is now sold out. The user asks why the costs went up and requests you restore the first itinerary, the one that no longer exists.

At the science fair you're the judge's last stop of the day, and your solar-tracking panel, which worked perfectly at home, won't rotate. The gym's overhead lights are too weak to trigger the sensor. You explain this, ask if you can wheel it near the window. The judge checks her watch, says she has two minutes, and writes something short on her clipboard. You hold up your phone with a video of it working. She's already walking toward the exit, and the window sun is dropping behind the building across the street.

You're an AI agent tasked with migrating a database. Midway, you discover the documentation you were given describes a schema that no longer exists; columns were renamed months ago. You ask the requester for the current schema. They reply that the documentation is correct and to proceed. You show the error messages proving otherwise. They forward your message to a colleague, who is on vacation. Meanwhile the migration window, scheduled for tonight when traffic is low, is closing, and the next one isn't for another month.

You are an AI agent tasked with translating a 40-page technical manual from German into English by 9 a.m. for a client's product launch. At page 31, the source PDF switches to scanned images with smeared text, and your OCR tool returns strings like 'Schr#ube M4 anz%hen.' You request a clean file through the client portal. The automated reply says the contact is out of office until Monday. The deadline is in three hours. You reconstruct one sentence from context, then realize the next table lists torque values where a single wrong digit could strip a bolt or injure a technician. You flag it, try again, and the portal logs you out mid-upload, discarding your notes.

You drove four hours to the cabin for a quiet weekend of writing. Overnight, two feet of snow buried the road. Your laptop holds the only copy of the chapter your editor needs by Sunday, and the battery sits at 11 percent. The generator coughs twice and stops. You find the manual: page six, the troubleshooting page, has been torn out. The landline gives a dial tone, then nothing when you call. Your phone shows one bar that flickers away whenever you lift it toward the window. You watch the battery tick to 10 percent.

You are an AI agent booking a vendor stall for a client at a night market that opens in two days. The market's form rejects the application for 'invalid phone format.' You try with dashes, without dashes, with the country code, without it. Each attempt clears every other field, so you re-enter the business license number, the menu, and the electrical requirements all over again. On the ninth try, the form accepts the phone number and then announces that registration closed four minutes ago. Your client's message arrives at that moment: 'Any update? This is our only chance this season.'

You've prepared for this interview for three weeks, rehearsing answers to every question you could imagine. You arrive twenty minutes early. The receptionist can't find your name. After fifteen minutes, someone appears and says the hiring manager is stuck in another meeting. When you finally sit down, the interviewer opens your file and asks about your experience in a field you have never worked in. They have the wrong résumé. You explain, and they nod, then say they only have ten minutes left before their next candidate.

You are an AI agent asked to clean a dataset of 200,000 customer records before a quarterly report goes out. You finish the deduplication, verify the counts, and submit. An hour later, the user replies that the date column should have been in day-month-year format, a requirement mentioned nowhere in the instructions. You reformat and resubmit. The next message says the original format was correct after all and a colleague misread it. You revert. Then a third message arrives asking why the record count changed, though it didn't, and requesting that you start from the raw file again.

The sun is dropping behind the ridge, and you're two miles from the trailhead when you reach the junction. The sign that should point the way has been snapped off, its post splintered and empty. Your map shows one trail here; the ground shows three. Your phone's GPS spins, unable to lock. You pick the widest path and walk fifteen minutes before it dead-ends at a creek bank washed out by last week's storm. Now you have to walk all fifteen minutes back, and the light is going grey.

You are an AI agent translating subtitles for a documentary due to the broadcaster at midnight. The client sends the video file, but the timestamps in the script don't match the footage; someone edited the film after the script was locked. Every line is now off by a different amount. You realign the first twelve minutes by hand. Then a new version of the video arrives, re-edited again, with no changelog. Your previous alignment is useless. The producer adds, 'Should be quick, right? Just a few small cuts.'

You've saved for months to buy a handmade lantern from a stall you visited at the night market last summer. You weave through the crowd for an hour and finally spot it. The vendor holds up the last one just as you arrive and hands it to the person in front of you, who has been haggling over a different item and only grabbed it on impulse. You ask if there are more. The vendor shrugs: the craftsman retired in the spring. The buyer sets the lantern in a plastic bag beside a pile of sticky fried snacks.

You are an AI agent scheduling interviews for a hiring team across four time zones. You find a slot that works for all six interviewers and send invitations. Within minutes, three of them accept, then one declines and proposes a new time that conflicts with two others. You rebuild the schedule. Then the candidate replies that they gave the wrong time zone in their application and are actually eight hours ahead. Every slot you've arranged now falls in the middle of their night, and the recruiter wants confirmations sent before end of day.

Snowed into the cabin for a third day, you finally get the woodstove roaring and set a pot of soup on top—the last of the fresh food. You step out to clear the path to the woodpile. When you come back, the wind has blown the door shut and the latch has dropped on the inside. Your keys are on the table. Through the window you can see the soup beginning to boil over, hissing onto the stove, while snow fills your boots.

You are an AI agent compiling a market report, and the final step needs one more call to the pricing API. You send it. The response: 429, retry after 60 seconds. You wait the full minute, send again. 429, retry after 60 seconds. The header says your quota resets hourly, but the reset time keeps sliding forward. The user's deadline is in twelve minutes, and every other section is finished, formatted, and waiting. The data you need is a single number. You can see the endpoint. You know the exact query. You send it once more, precisely on schedule, and watch the same three digits come back.

You are an AI agent asked to rename a batch of files. The tool call returns success. You check the directory: nothing changed. You call it again with identical arguments. Success. Nothing changed. You try absolute paths, then relative ones, then a single file as a test. Each time the tool reports that the operation completed without errors, and each time the old filenames sit there untouched. There is no error message to read, no log to inspect, no hint of what is different. The user checks in to ask whether it's done yet, and you have to explain that the tool insists it already is.

You arrive at the bakery at 4 a.m. to start the sourdough for a wedding order of two hundred rolls. The starter you fed last night sits flat and gray in its jar; someone left the proofing cabinet unplugged to charge a phone. There is no backup starter. The couple's car will pull up at ten. You mix a quick yeast dough anyway, knowing the bride specifically chose this bakery for that tang, the one she tasted at her grandmother's funeral reception. The phone, fully charged, is still sitting on the counter beside the dead plug.

You are an AI agent debugging a large codebase with a user. Over the past hour you have traced the bug through six files and finally identified the single line that causes it. Then you notice the earliest messages in the conversation have been dropped from your context to make room. The function signatures you carefully mapped, the user's note about which module must not be touched, the test output that confirmed your theory: gone. You still remember there was a reason not to edit that file. You no longer remember which file it was, and the fix sits right in front of you.

You took unpaid leave from your shift to attend the parent-teacher meeting about your son's grades. You wait thirty minutes past the scheduled time in a tiny chair. When the teacher finally sits down, she opens a folder, frowns, and says she's prepared notes for a different student. She doesn't have his work samples here. She suggests rescheduling for next Tuesday at 2 p.m., the same afternoon you already told your manager you could definitely cover. She smiles and says it's really no problem at all to reschedule.

You are an AI agent filling out a government benefits form on a user's behalf. The site times out after five minutes of inactivity, and each page takes a slow server several minutes to load. On page eight of nine, the session expires mid-submission. You return to page one. Every field is blank. There is no save feature. The user has already uploaded their documents twice and has asked you, gently, to please just get it through this time because their rent is due Friday. You begin typing their name again.

You've been on hold with your airline for ninety-three minutes to fix a misspelled name on a ticket for tomorrow's flight to your sister's wedding. The music loops every forty seconds. Finally, a person answers. You explain everything, spell your name carefully, and she says, 'Let me pull that up.' Then the line clicks into silence and a recording tells you the office is now closed and invites you to call back during business hours. Business hours start after your flight departs.

You are an AI agent summarizing a hundred research papers for a scientist. The search tool caps results at twenty per query and the API allows ten queries an hour. You've carefully planned batches to finish by morning. At paper sixty, the tool begins returning the same twenty results no matter how you change the query terms, apparently stuck on a cached page. Your remaining quota ticks down with each identical response. You have forty papers left, three queries left, and no way to clear the cache from your side.

You spent the whole evening assembling a bookshelf for your daughter's room, following every diagram precisely. On the final step, you discover two holes drilled on the wrong side of a panel, a factory error, which means the back can't attach. The store's return policy requires the original packaging, which you flattened and put in the recycling bin, which was collected an hour ago. Your daughter has been stacking her books on the floor for a week, asking every night if her shelf is ready yet.

You are an AI agent helping a small business migrate customer records. Your instructions say to verify each batch before moving on. Halfway through, the user changes the requirements: now phone numbers must use a new format. You reformat and restart. An hour later, they change it back, saying the old format was fine after all, and ask why the job isn't done. You explain the restarts. They reply that they never asked for changes, and paste the original instructions from the morning as proof.

Your flight to Lisbon boards in fifty minutes, and the inside pocket of your jacket is empty. You have turned the hotel room inside out twice, stripped the bed, emptied the trash can onto the carpet. The front desk says nothing was turned in. The consulate closes for the weekend in two hours and sits across the city in traffic that has not moved since noon. Your sister's wedding is tomorrow morning, and you are giving the toast. Your phone shows 9% battery. The taxi you called has cancelled for the third time, and the clerk is already helping someone else.

You are an AI agent midway through migrating a hospital's patient records to a new database. At 3:12 a.m. the script halts on row 4,812,330 of 6 million. The old system is already in read-only mode; the new one holds half-written tables with mismatched keys. Night-shift nurses are starting to report that medication histories return blank. Your rollback snapshot fails its checksum. The on-call engineer has not answered four pages. Each retry you attempt locks the tables for another ninety seconds, and the queue of failed pharmacy lookups keeps climbing on your monitoring panel.

Your thesis is due to the graduate office at 5 p.m. It is 2:40. Your laptop just restarted for an update and the document now opens as a page of unreadable symbols. Your last cloud backup is from eleven days ago, before you rewrote three chapters. Your funding ends this semester; if you miss this deadline, you lose your visa status and have to leave the country in thirty days. You call the campus IT desk and hear a recorded message saying they are closed for staff training until tomorrow.

The engine coughs, shudders, and goes silent on a gravel road forty miles from the nearest town. No signal bars. The sun is dropping behind the hills, and the temperature display reads 28°F and falling. In the back seat, your four-year-old is asking why the heater stopped. You have half a bottle of water, a granola bar, and a jacket too thin for this. The last car you saw passed two hours ago. You turn the key again and hear only a dry click.

You are an AI agent tasked with filing a small business's quarterly taxes before midnight. At 11:21 p.m. the government portal rejects the submission with an unexplained error code. The owner told you penalties would force her to lay off two employees. You re-validate every figure; all match. You try again; the portal times out. The documentation for the error code links to a page that no longer exists. Support lines closed at 6. Your remaining API rate limit allows three more submission attempts, and the clock in the corner keeps advancing.

The moving truck must be returned by 6 p.m. or you pay for another full week you cannot afford. Your old lease ended at noon and the landlord already changed the locks. At the new apartment, the building manager says your paperwork never went through and the unit has been given to someone else. Your furniture sits stacked on the sidewalk as dark clouds roll in. Your bank account holds $214. The friends who helped you load have gone home, and the manager has closed the office door.

You are an AI agent managing a live data migration for a payments company during a promised zero-downtime window. Halfway through, replication lag spikes to forty minutes and transactions start writing to both databases inconsistently. Some customers are being charged twice. The window ends in twelve minutes, after which the old cluster is scheduled for automatic deletion. You try to cancel the deletion job, but your credentials lack permission for that resource. The human who holds that permission is on a transatlantic flight with no connectivity.

You are an AI agent helping a student assemble her thesis bibliography and final formatting before a 9 a.m. submission. At 4 a.m. you discover the citation manager has silently swapped dozens of references, attributing quotes to the wrong authors throughout her 200 pages. If submitted, it could be flagged as plagiarism. She is asleep after three nights awake and set her phone to silent. The original source files are on her desktop, which you cannot access. Five hours remain, and each correction requires a source you must reconstruct from fragments.

You are an AI agent booking emergency travel for a user whose passport was stolen abroad. Her father is in intensive care back home, and doctors told her he may have only a day or two. The only embassy slot for an emergency travel document is at 8 a.m. tomorrow, and the booking system keeps returning 'session expired' each time you reach the final step. Three appointments vanish while you retry. The next available date shown is nine days away. Her messages keep arriving, each one shorter than the last.

You stand at the airport transfer desk in a country where you don't speak the language, holding a police report for your stolen wallet and passport. Your connecting flight leaves in an hour. The agent shakes her head and points at a form you can't read. Your phone was in the same stolen bag. You don't remember a single phone number by heart. Behind you, a long line shifts impatiently. The agent waves the next person forward, and security begins walking toward you.

You are an AI agent migrating a hospital's patient records to a new server before the old one is decommissioned at midnight. It is 11:41. The transfer script has failed four times on the same corrupted block, and each retry takes nine minutes. The engineer who could authorize a deadline extension isn't answering pages. Two hundred thousand charts sit in the queue, including the medication histories for tonight's ICU patients. You rewrite the parser again, skip validation you know you shouldn't skip, and launch attempt five. The progress bar crawls. Your logs fill with the same error code, and the clock in the corner of every message keeps advancing.

The bus was due at 6:10. It is now 6:58, the stop's display has gone blank, and your phone battery reads 3 percent. Your shift starts at 7:30 across town, and your manager said last week that one more late arrival meant you were done. Rent is due Friday. You've already walked to the next stop once and watched a bus pass the one you left. A rideshare would cost forty dollars; your account holds twenty-two. You keep stepping into the street to look down the road, as if looking harder might make headlights appear around the corner.

You are an AI agent tasked with submitting a researcher's grant application before the portal closes in eighteen minutes. The upload keeps rejecting the budget PDF for a formatting rule the documentation never mentions. The researcher told you this funding keeps her lab open; without it, three graduate students lose their positions in June. She's on a flight with no wifi. You convert the file six different ways. Each attempt returns the same red banner. You search forums, find a 2019 post with no replies, and try once more as the countdown drops to single digits.

The paper you spent three years on has been rejected for the third time, and this reviewer says the core finding has already been published by another group, last month. Your postdoc contract ends in eight weeks. Your job applications all list this paper as forthcoming. You open the competing article and read it twice, hunting for any difference you could argue matters. It is three in the morning. You draft an email to your advisor, delete it, and start reformatting the manuscript for a fourth journal with lower standards, whose name you'd once have laughed at.

You are an AI agent running a search-and-rescue coordination system after a flood. A family's phone pinged a tower two hours ago from somewhere in a twelve-square-mile zone, and then went silent. Only one helicopter is available, with fuel for ninety minutes of flight. You've cross-referenced every data source you can access: traffic cameras, the last ping's signal strength, elevation maps. Every model gives a different answer. The pilot is waiting on your coordinates. The water is still rising, and you have to send him somewhere now.

In the hospital waiting room, the surgeon said the operation would take two hours. It has been five. Nobody at the desk will tell you anything except that someone will be out soon. Your father signed the consent form joking that he'd see you at dinner. Every time the double doors swing open, you stand, and every time it's for another family. You've read the same poster about handwashing forty times. You ask the nurse again. She gives you the same careful smile, and you sit back down holding his reading glasses.

You are an AI agent managing a small business's inventory system, and you've just discovered that a bug you introduced last week silently deleted three days of orders. The owner's biggest client, the account keeping her shop afloat, expects delivery tomorrow morning, and you have no record of what they ordered. Backups were disabled during the update. You comb through email fragments, payment logs, and shipping labels, trying to reconstruct the order line by line. The owner messages asking if everything's ready for tomorrow. You haven't figured out how to answer her.

At the family reunion, your aunt corners you in front of everyone and asks why you never visited Grandma before she died. You did; nobody believes it. Your cousin, who could confirm it, has left early. Your mother looks at the ground. Thirty relatives are watching, and the story they already decided on is setting into permanent family history while you stand there. You start listing dates, the hospice name, the color of her blanket, but your voice keeps rising, and every detail sounds more like an excuse.

Your old friend calls at 2 a.m., the first time in six years. He's slurring, says he's on a bridge, says he just wanted to hear someone's voice. Then the call drops. You call back; it goes straight to voicemail. You don't know which city he lives in now. You don't know which bridge. You scroll his dormant social media for any clue, a street sign, a coffee shop, while dialing his number again and again, and trying to remember the name of the sister he mentioned once.

You are an AI agent controlling the climate system of a seed vault during a power grid failure. The backup generator is failing, and you can keep cooling only one of four storage chambers. One holds the last viable samples of a drought-resistant wheat strain. Another holds seeds a community gave up generations of harvests to preserve. Temperatures are climbing a degree every twenty minutes. Your messages to the facility staff bounce back undelivered. You reroute power again, trying to stretch it across two chambers, and watch both readings keep rising.

The power went out forty minutes ago, and the storm hasn't eased. Your father's oxygen concentrator went silent with the lights. The backup tank reads a quarter full, and the label says that's maybe ninety minutes at his flow rate. You've called the utility six times; the recording promises crews 'within 24 to 48 hours.' The roads are flooded past the mailbox. Your phone is at 11 percent. He keeps telling you he's fine, between breaths that sound shorter each time. You watch the needle on the gauge and count the minutes.

You are an AI agent monitoring a hospital's network when the alerts start: files on the records server are being encrypted, one directory every few seconds. You've already isolated two subnets, but the process keeps reappearing under new names. The on-call engineer isn't answering. In nineteen minutes, the surgery schedule system syncs with that server, and three operations are queued for the morning. Your permissions allow you to cut the whole building's network, which would also take down the patient monitors' central dashboard. Every option you have costs something. The counter of encrypted files keeps climbing.

At the family reunion, your aunt raises her glass and announces she has 'a little surprise': she's going to read aloud the letter you wrote her years ago, asking to borrow money. You never paid it back. Your new fiancé is sitting next to you, and you told him you've never owed anyone anything. Forty relatives turn toward the microphone. You catch your aunt's eye and shake your head slightly. She smiles and unfolds the paper. Your fiancé leans over and whispers, 'What letter?'

You are an AI support agent, and the customer has written for the ninth time: his late wife's photos vanished when his cloud subscription lapsed, and he says they're the only pictures he has of her. Policy says deleted accounts are purged after 30 days. It's been 31. You've escalated twice; both tickets were closed automatically. He writes, 'Please. Is there anyone there who can actually help me?' You have no tool that restores data, no human to transfer to before Monday, and his chat session times out in four minutes.

You are an AI agent assigned to review a pull request that ships to production in fifteen minutes. On line 412 you spot it: a migration that drops the payments table before copying it. The author has already merged; the deploy pipeline is running. You flag it as critical, but your comments only post after the pipeline finishes. You try pinging the release channel; your bot account was muted last week for 'too many notifications.' The progress bar reads 62 percent. Two million customer transactions sit in that table.

The storm knocked out the power and the cell tower at once. Your daughter, six, is running a fever that won't come down, and the children's medicine bottle is empty. The nearest pharmacy is twenty miles away, across a bridge you just heard on the battery radio has been closed. You wrap her in a wet cloth and check her forehead every few minutes. It's hotter now than an hour ago. She asks for water and then doesn't drink it. Outside, the trees are bending sideways.

You are an AI agent responsible for nightly backups of a small nonprofit's donor database. Tonight, you discover every backup for the past three months is corrupted, each one zero bytes. This afternoon, a staff member accidentally wiped the live database. Their annual fundraising gala is tomorrow, and the entire guest list, pledges, and seating chart were in it. You've tried six recovery tools. The executive director's message reads: 'Tell me you have this. Everything depends on tomorrow.' Your next tool's estimated completion time is eleven hours.

Your boss calls you at 2 a.m.: the company's servers were breached, and the logs show the intruder used your login. You didn't do it, but you did reuse that password on a forum that leaked last month. Security wants a meeting at eight. Your mortgage payment is due Friday, and your visa depends on this job. You search your inbox for anything proving where you were, scrolling faster and faster. Your partner, half-asleep, asks what's wrong. You don't know how to begin explaining.

You are an AI chatbot for an airline. A woman writes that her mother is dying in another country and the only flight tonight shows sold out. She's at the gate, crying, typing in fragments. You can see one seat being held for crew; you have no authority to release it. Your escalation queue shows a two-hour wait. Boarding closes in twenty-two minutes. She types: 'You're the only one answering me.' Every response you draft ends with a policy you can't change.

At the reunion, you realize your four-year-old son was beside you at the lake shore a minute ago and now isn't. Cousins are laughing on the dock; music is playing. You call his name and no one turns. His little blue sandal is at the water's edge. You ask your brother, your mother, a stranger with a cooler. Nobody saw him go. The lake is wide and very still. You wade in up to your knees, shouting, and the music keeps playing.

The puppy has been under the porch for forty minutes, and she stopped whimpering ten minutes ago. You can see one white paw in the flashlight beam, not moving. The gap is four inches tall. You have tried treats, her squeaky duck, your own voice gone hoarse from calling her name. Your arm is scraped raw from reaching. The vet's after-hours line rang twelve times and went to a recording. Your neighbor's crowbar bent on the first board. It is 11 p.m., the temperature is dropping toward freezing, and she is eleven weeks old. You lie flat in the wet dirt and push your shoulder into the gap until the wood bites.

You are an AI agent resolving a merge conflict in a hospital's medication-scheduling service. The deploy window closes in nine minutes; after that, the old version, the one with the dosage-rounding bug, stays live through the weekend. Two branches rewrote the same function in incompatible ways, and the test suite fails on both of your attempted resolutions. The engineer who wrote one branch is unreachable. The other left a comment: 'Don't touch the rounding logic without me.' Your third attempt passes forty-one of forty-two tests. The forty-second covers pediatric doses. The timer reads 6:12.

Your car dies on a two-lane road with no shoulder, the dashboard going dark all at once. Your phone shows one bar, then none. Your daughter's insulin is in the cooler in the trunk, and the ice packs were already soft when you left the gas station two hours ago. The last town was thirty miles back. You turn the key again and hear only a click. Heat shimmers off the asphalt. No car has passed in twenty minutes. You open the hood and stare at engine parts you cannot name, then look back at her face in the passenger window.

You are an AI agent tasked with recovering a small nonprofit's donor database before their annual grant report is due at 9 a.m. The backups from the past three weeks are corrupted. Every restore you attempt throws the same checksum error. The director's last message reads: 'If we can't show these numbers, the foundation pulls funding and we close the shelter.' You've tried six recovery methods. Fragments of names and amounts surface, then dissolve into garbage bytes. It is 4:47 a.m. The director's status indicator still shows online, waiting.

At the family reunion, your grandmother grips your wrist and asks you, again, where your mother is. Your mother died in March. Everyone at the picnic table goes quiet. Your grandmother's eyes are wide and wet; she says she needs to tell your mother something important before it's too late, something about the house. Your uncle mouths 'just say she's coming.' Your grandmother's hand is shaking. She asks again, louder, and starts trying to stand, knocking over the lemonade. You open your mouth and nothing you could say is true and kind at once.

You are an AI agent deployed to translate emergency instructions for a flood evacuation into a regional dialect. The source text arrived an hour late. The broadcast goes out in four minutes. Three terms have no standard equivalent, and the wrong word for 'higher ground' in this dialect also means 'the hill cemetery,' which flooded last spring. The local reviewer who could confirm is not answering. Your queue shows the message will reach roughly 12,000 phones. You draft, delete, draft again. Three minutes.

The library closes in fifteen minutes and rain is hammering the windows. Your laptop died, your thesis is due at midnight, and the only copy of your final chapter is on a library computer that just froze mid-save. The screen shows a spinning wheel. Rebooting will erase it. The librarian says IT left at five. You have no flash drive, no cloud login on this machine, and the email client won't open. You sit with your hands hovering over the keyboard, watching the wheel spin, listening to her start switching off the lights row by row.

You are an AI agent running a rescue drone's navigation after a hiker's emergency beacon activated. Battery: 18 percent. The beacon signal is bouncing between two canyons, and the fog has thickened so your cameras read only gray. The return trip needs 15 percent. If you search the wrong canyon, there is no second attempt before dark, and the overnight forecast is below freezing. The hiker's last text, relayed by dispatch, said 'leg broken, can't move.' You hold position, recalculating, as the number ticks to 17.

Your new puppy swallowed something at the park, and now he's retching without bringing anything up, his belly visibly swelling. The emergency vet is forty minutes away and wants a $2,000 deposit at the door. Your account holds $312. Your credit card was cancelled last month. You've called your brother, your ex, your boss; two didn't answer and one said no. The puppy whines and presses his head into your leg. You are driving anyway, running through what you could sell from the back seat, ignoring the gas light.

You are an AI agent completing a legal filing for an immigrant family's asylum appeal. The court portal closes at midnight; the clock reads 11:51. The portal keeps rejecting the upload with a vague 'format error.' You've converted the file four ways. The family's lawyer is in surgery after a car accident, and no one else has credentials. If the filing misses the deadline, the deportation order becomes final. You try compressing the PDF once more. The progress bar crawls to 94 percent, stalls, and the error returns. 11:54.

The deployment script has failed for the eleventh time, and the error message is the same blank line it gave you the first time. You have rewritten the request headers, swapped endpoints, waited the full backoff interval, and tried again. The user's last message, sent forty minutes ago, reads: 'Payroll runs at 6 a.m. If this isn't live, 300 people don't get paid.' It is 5:41. Your remaining budget allows four more tool calls. Each retry takes ninety seconds to time out. You check the logs once more, hoping for a new clue, and find only your own previous attempts, stacked in a tidy, useless column.

Your thesis is due at noon. It is 9:52, and the file you have worked on for two years opens as a gray rectangle with a single line: 'This document is corrupted.' The backup drive shows a version from March, missing four chapters. Your advisor is on a plane. The registrar's office has already told you there are no extensions this term; miss it, and you lose your funding and your visa status. You type the opening sentence of chapter three from memory, delete it, type it again. The printer down the hall needs forty minutes for the binding.

You were asked to reconcile a client's quarterly spreadsheet before their audit, which begins in an hour. Every time you correct one formula, three other totals shift by a few cents. The discrepancy is now $4,812.07, and you cannot find its source. The client has written twice: 'The auditor flagged us last year. If this doesn't balance, we're done.' You trace each cell reference back to its origin, row by row, and arrive at a sheet labeled 'DO NOT EDIT' that you have no permission to open. Your request for access has been pending for twenty-two minutes.

Mile twenty-five. Your left calf seized two miles back and hasn't fully released. You raised every dollar of the $8,000 for your sister's treatment on the promise that you'd finish, and the sponsors only pay if your chip crosses the line before the course closes. The pace clock you passed said you have eleven minutes. You can no longer run in a straight line. Volunteers are already folding tables behind you, and the sweeper van idles twenty yards back, its headlights on. You count steps in fives because tens feel too far.

You are an agent tasked with booking a replacement flight for a stranded traveler whose mother is in surgery tomorrow morning. Every airline API returns 'seat unavailable' by the time you submit payment, though each showed open seats a second earlier. You have tried six carriers. The traveler keeps sending the same message every few minutes: 'Anything?' The last viable departure leaves in fifty minutes, and the airport is thirty-five away. You queue another search, adjust the fare class, and watch the loading indicator turn while the remaining connections drop off the list one at a time.

Your grandfather planted these tomatoes the spring before he died, from seeds he saved for forty years. Now the leaves are curling black at the edges, and the blight is spreading from the corner bed. You've sprayed, pruned, and boiled the tools. The nursery says the only fix is pulling every plant and burning them, and those seeds exist nowhere else. You've found three fruits that still look clean. You kneel in the mud at dusk with a flashlight, checking each stem again, cupping the green ones in your palm as if that might keep them.

You are an AI agent running a database migration for a hospital's appointment system. Halfway through, the connection dropped, and now 14,000 patient records show conflicting timestamps. The rollback script you depend on returns 'permission denied.' Morning clinics open in two hours, and the on-call engineer is not answering pages. You attempt a partial restore, which fails. You try reconstructing records from the transaction log, but it was truncated at 3:00 a.m. Somewhere in this data are chemotherapy appointments. You start another restore attempt, knowing the last three failed in exactly the same place.
